reason: The Interactions presence_penalty/frequency_penalty and cached_content fields first appeared in 2.9.0 (2026-06-19) and are absent from 2.7.0, the last release before 2026-06-01, so no code written for the old version uses them (and cached_content is still accepted, deprecated, in 2.30.0); tried the Interactions create params and GenerationConfig in 2.7.0, 2.8.0, 2.9.0 and 2.10.0.

The old behavior only shows once a request runs past undici's 300 s default headers/body timeout (2.7.0 leaves those defaults in place when no timeout is given; 2.30.0 disables them per request), far beyond the 60 s budget, and code that sets an explicit timeout behaves the same on both.

A transport tuning default (the HTTP/2 flow-control window of Firestore's Node gRPC channel) that changes throughput only; no result an application sees depends on it, and observing it would also need a Firestore backend.

initializeAppCheck() without a provider existed only in 12.15.0 (2026-06-16); in 12.14.0, the last release before 2026-06-01, AppCheckOptions.provider is required exactly as in 13.0.0 (identical declarations), so no code written for the old version is affected.

Code written for 2.7.0 passes the environment network as an inline { allowlist: [{ domain, transform }] } object, which 2.30.0 still accepts (network is typed EnvironmentNetworkEgressAllowlist | 'disabled') and sends unchanged; only an annotation naming 2.7.0's Interactions.Environment.Allowlist type breaks, and that name was already gone before 2.28.0 (tried both against 2.30.0).

Interactions.Arguments and Interactions.RetrievalType first appear in 2.9.0/2.10.0 and are absent from 2.7.0, the last release before 2026-06-01 (which already exports URLContextCallArguments), so no code written for the old version names them.

response_modalities is set in the request object passed to interactions.create(), and TypeScript reports its @deprecated tag only on property reads, not on object-literal properties (checked with the typescript-6 suggestion diagnostics: no 6385/6387 for create({ ..., response_modalities: ["image"] })), and the SDK emits no runtime warning for it.
